Therefore, this paper introduces a multi-channel high speed sorting control scheme based on FPGA, which realizes high-speed bus communication protocols through high-performance CPUs embedded within the chip, and designs multi-channel parallel material rejection sensor control logic through the programmable logic features of FPGA, thereby improving the precision and parallel processing efficiency of material rejection control. This significantly enhances the sorting accuracy and production capacity of the sorting equipment.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Fusion Method of Multi-Source Heterogeneous Data for Inter-Area Pumped Storage Plant Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Due to the variety of data sources, there may be problems of uneven data quality, such as different data accuracy, inconsistent data format, missing or incorrect data, etc., which will affect the effectiveness and accuracy of data fusion. Therefore, this study aims to propose an adaptive fusion method of heterogeneous data from multiple sources for the operation of cross-area pumped storage power plants, in order to achieve comprehensive and accurate integration and analysis of power plant operation data. Firstly, a data acquisition and transmission system is established for multiple regions and multiple data sources involved in pumped storage power plants to achieve real-time acquisition and transmission of various data. Then, data fusion algorithms and models are designed to adaptively fuse data from different sources by taking into account the heterogeneity and spatial and temporal characteristics of the data, in order to obtain more comprehensive and accurate information about the operating status of the power plant. Then, the adaptive fusion of heterogeneous data from multiple sources is realised by combining data mining and machine learning techniques. The experimental results show that the security management of data can be strengthened by fusion technology to prevent data leakage and misuse and to guarantee the security of data. In addition, by fusing data from different sources, the supply and demand situation of the power system can be analysed more accurately, so as to achieve better resource allocation and improve the efficiency of energy use.

articleTitle: Injury Monitoring of Underground Structure Based on Optical Fiber Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Under extreme conditions, ensuring the integrity and functionality of the underground infrastructure is critical for military and industrial applications, especially for the real-time monitoring and assessment of post-explosion structures. In recent years, sensor technology has gained wide attention in the field of structural health monitoring, including strain gauges, accelerometers, piezoelectric ceramic sheets, and piezoelectric thin film sensors. In particular, distributed fiber sensors are widely used in the field of civil engineering with their high sensitivity and long-distance monitoring capabilities. However, the current research on the performance evaluation of reinforced concrete structures under explosive load is relatively limited, and most applications focus on the monitoring of conventional impact and pressurized load. This paper presents a new method based on distributed fiber sensing technology to detect the damage of reinforced concrete slab under explosive load, realizes the qualitative damage monitoring of RC slab, and discusses the future research direction. The experimental results show that the distributed fiber sensor can effectively monitor the integrity of the structure under the explosion load, and the monitoring results are consistent with the observed structural damage. This study will provide a new research idea for the damage assessment of the reinforced concrete structure under the explosion load.

Author Keywords: distributed optical fiber optic sensing technology

articleTitle: Low-computation Online Calibration Method for Accelerometer Size-effect in RINS
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: When carrier undergoes attitude motion, the size-effect errors of accelerometer will lead to the deterioration of positioning accuracy in rotational inertial navigation system (RINS), which are necessary to be calibrated and compensated before putting into operation. The published calibration methods are usually based on establishing high-dimensional Kalman filter models, which have the disadvantages of large computational complexity, long computation time, and difficulty in online operation. In this paper, a novel low-computation calibration method for accelerometer size-effect errors is proposed, which combines the advantages of analytical calibration and Kalman filter calibration methods. The simulation and experiments prove that the proposed method can effectively calibrate the size-effect errors, with calibration accuracy better than 1 mm and the time cost shorter than 35 min. By comparing with the high-dimensional filtering calibration method, the proposed method has only one tenth of the computational complexity, which can realize the online calibration and greatly improve the maintenance efficiency of RINS.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of High-Pressure Sensitivity Irregular Side-hole Fiber Based on Fiber Bragg Grating Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: The pressure sensor based on Side-hole Fiber Bragg Grating (SH-FBG) can effectively reduce the crosstalk between pressure and temperature in operation, making it particularly suitable for high-temperature and high-pressure environments in oil wells. However, the relatively low sensitivity of SHF pressure sensors limits their further application in oil wells. In this paper, the key to improving the sensitivity of SHF pressure sensors is theoretically derived to be the increase in the unevenness of stress generated at the core in the $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ directions. Finite element analysis is then employed to investigate the influence of SHF cladding shape on pressure sensing characteristics. By optimizing the waveguide structure of SHF and proposing an Irregular Side-hole Fiber (ISHF) with a cladding shape of negative curvature arc, the pressure sensitivity is increased to $33.37 \mathrm{pm} / \mathrm{MPa}$. This effectively enhances the pressure sensitivity of SHF, holding significant implications for high-pressure monitoring in oil wells.

articleTitle: Design of automatic docking controller based on probe and drogue aerial refueling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: In the process of probe and drogue aerial refueling, the docking and refueling stage have the highest requirements for precision, safety and efficiency, and the control is extremely difficult, which is an important part of the design of automatic air refueling flight control system. This paper studies how to control the receiver to achieve close-range accurate air docking control after the receiver completes the rendezvous with the tanker and reaches the close-range formation position below the side and back of the tanker. In this paper, the reference observer based tracking controller (ROTC) method is used to design the docking controller of the receiver. According to the relative position between the receiver and the tanker measured by the sensor, the ideal state information and control information that the receiver needs to track are estimated by the reference observer, and then the flight control system of the receiver is designed by the full state feedback to realize the docking and refueling maintenance between the receiver probe and the refueling drogue.

articleTitle: A Wearable Indentation System for Accurately Monitoring Young’s Modulus of Soft Tissues
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Tissue stiffness can reflect the development of tissue lesions, changes in muscle strength, and muscle injuries. While accurate evaluation of tissue stiffness is valuable for monitoring these conditions, it remains a significant challenge. Here we developed a wearable tissue stiffness monitoring system (WSMS) to accurately evaluate the changes of tissue’s Young’s modulus through simultaneous measuring of the contact force and contact radius of the interface between a spherical indenter and the tissue via tactile sensing array. The WSMS, with dimensions of $\mathbf{2 6 ~ m m} \times$ $\mathbf{2 3} \mathbf{~ m m} \times 23 \mathrm{~mm}$, can be secured to human body with straps to measure the Young’s modulus of tissues. The WSMS demonstrated high accuracy in detecting the Young’s modulus of five custom-made PDMS cylinders with varying stiffness, achieving an average absolute error of less than 6 kPa and an overall accuracy of $\mathbf{9 3 \%}$. The WSMS shows great potential as an effective tool for the diagnosis, evaluation, and rehabilitation monitoring of related diseases.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enhanced Smart Sensors for Hand Gesture Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Against the backdrop of highly developed smart sensor technology, machine learning, and multimodal data analysis, hand gesture recognition (HGR) has become an important field in promoting human-computer interaction, health monitoring, and rehabilitation medicine. This paper proposes a smart sensor system based on machine learning enhancement, which combines hardware devices such as Flex sensor, JY901S, camera and smart gloves, as well as machine learning models such as support vector machine (SVM) and long short-term memory network (LSTM), using For processing and analysis of gesture data. By using multi-modal data in static and dynamic gesture classification tasks, experimental results show that collaborative inference of multi-modal data significantly improves the model’s classification accuracy compared to single or bi-modal data.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Integrated and Autonomously Controllable Metal Detection System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated and autonomously controllable metal detection system. Throughout the research, a combination of theoretical analysis, simulation modeling, and experimental validation has been employed as methodological tools to comprehensively evaluate the system’s performance in real-world scenarios, with particular emphasis on its stability and accuracy under dynamic operating conditions. A series of rigorous tests and data analyses demonstrate that the designed system not only maintains robust operational stability across complex and variable application environments but also achieves high precision in localization.

articleTitle: Optimization of Narrow-magnet EMAT for Lamb Waves with Low Distortion
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Compared to traditional electromagnetic acoustic transducer (EMAT), the narrow-magnet EMAT extends its meander conductors to the edges and outside of the magnet, hence a wider area of the magnetic field can be used to excite stronger ultrasound waves. Because of the magnetic field inhomogeneity, the classical half-wavelength spacing rule is not suitable for the coil used in the narrow-magnet EMAT. Otherwise, obvious waveform distortions will appear. In this work, the coil conductor spacing correction methodology proposed in previous works is testified for Lamb wave excitations, and a simpler wavelength-based adjustment approach is proposed, where waveforms of low distortions can be obtained. Both approaches are evaluated in simulation and practical experiments, where the Lamb wave amplitude enhancement brought by the coil conductor spacing correction method is more than 157.41%, and the improvement achieved by the proposed wavelength adjustment concept is above 179.34%.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor Deep Fusion Perception Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: This study proposes a deep object detection method based on the fusion of multi-line LiDAR point cloud data and RGB images to improve detection accuracy and system robustness in autonomous driving environments. The method first performs feature extraction and deep fusion of multi-line LiDAR and image data, combining candidate object extraction and 3D object detection to achieve precise spatial localization. Experimental results show that, compared to methods using image data alone, this fusion approach significantly improves performance across various detection tasks on the KITTI dataset, especially in terms of detection accuracy and adaptability in complex environments. Additionally, comparative analysis with state-of-the-art algorithms, YOLOv5 and Faster R-CNN, further validates the advantages of this method.

articleTitle: A Reliable Time Synchronization Scheme Based on Dynamic Selection of Extended Reference Nodes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: In large-scale wireless sensor networks (WSNs), sensor nodes achieve time synchronization by exchanging messages between reference nodes and sensor nodes. However, the presence of anomalous nodes may lead to unreliable timestamp messages, severely affecting the accuracy of time synchronization. Thus, this paper proposes a reliable time synchronization scheme based on the dynamic selection of extended reference nodes (DERS). Firstly, the scheme identifies the set of extended reference nodes, detects abnormal nodes using a listening mechanism, and dynamically selects high-priority extended reference nodes to perform time synchronization correction. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed time synchronization scheme effectively mitigates the impact of unreliable nodes, reduces synchronization energy consumption, and enhances the accuracy of time synchronization.

articleTitle: Design of a Fatigue Driving Warning System Utilizing Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Fatigue driving significantly threatens road safety in China, causing a large number of traffic accidents. Traditional fatigue detection methods, such as facial expression recognition, often fail to accurately reflect a driver’s cognitive state. This paper introduces a brain-computer interface (BCI)-based early warning system for detecting driver fatigue using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. The system, called the “Brain-Controlled Co-Pilot,” (BCCP) includes hardware for non-invasive EEG signal collection and amplification, along with software for signal processing, feature extraction, pattern recognition, and real-time analysis. By analyzing EEG signals, the system continuously monitors the driver’s attention level and issues timely alerts through visual, auditory, or tactile feedback when signs of fatigue are detected. The system also supports realtime data visualization and offers customizable settings for individual users. Experimental results confirm that the system effectively improves driver attention and reduces the risk of accidents caused by fatigue. The proposed BCI-based system holds significant potential for applications in health monitoring, virtual reality, education, smart homes, and driving safety.

articleTitle: An Novel Beidou Weak Signal Acquisition Method in Obstructed Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Signal acquisition is a critical step in the BeiDou satellite navigation system. In obstructed environments such as forest canopies or deep valleys, signals are often weakened due to multipath fading and shadowing effects, compounded by random noise. Traditional fixed-threshold detection methods struggle to achieve reliable acquisition under these conditions. To address this, a threshold-adaptive differential coherent accumulation algorithm is proposed in this paper. Firstly, based on the parallel phase acquisition algorithm, the proposed approach integrates a circular shifting algorithm and a differential coherent integration module. Furthermore, a noise power-based adaptive threshold detection method is introduced for decision making. MATLAB simulations and field tests in forest-obstructed environments demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves computational efficiency and signal acquisition probability compared to the parallel phase acquisition method.

articleTitle: PPO-CPG Controller for Quadruped Locomotion
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: The central pattern generator (CPG) can produce stable rhythmic signals for the locomotion of quadruped robots. However, the single CPG-based approach still requires further command tracking and movement stability enhancement due to its inherent lack of sensory feedback signals. In this paper, we proposed a PPO-CPG control architecture, which integrated deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques to enable the agent to modify the input parameters of the CPG network directly, thereby adjusting both the amplitude and frequency of gait output signals for achieving more stable and natural locomotion patterns. We conducted training within the Isaac Gym simulation environment and evaluated its performance on rough terrain conditions. The results indicated that our method reduces speed tracking error by approximately 55.45% compared to a single CPG-based method, demonstrating a significant improvement.

articleTitle: Glucowatch: A Novel Wearable Glucose Sensor Using Oxidative Reaction with Glucose Oxidase and Our Proposed Chemically Modified Biodegradable Origami-Inspired Paper Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel way to monitor glucose concentration during exercise using origami paper batteries with oxidative reactions from glucose oxidase. Origami designs allow for increased flexibility, durability, and surface-area-to-volume ratio, suitable for wearable sensors and increasing battery contact. This paper also utilizes chemical enhancements on the paper substrate to increase voltage production by using acid and base. The acid used was acetic acid to increase porosity, furthermore, increasing surface-area-to-volume ratio and increasing the overall battery contact as well as sodium hypochlorite base to increase conductivity. With these enhancements, there was an approximate increase of 10% increase of voltage. This paper uses its own composition of anode ink, cathode ink, and current collector, where the overall electrolyte was increased by adding polyethylene glycol, allowing for increased electron flow and being biodegradable. By increasing voltage production, the wearable sensor will be more sensitive and accurate to the glucose concentration present in the sweat. Using the Miura-Ori design, the folding angle was decreased to fit into a 2 inch by 3 inch frame of a conventional band aid. Comparing the usage of origami and chemically enhanced paper battery, it produced at least 4 times more voltages than no origami and nonchemically enhanced paper battery. This indicates that with chemical enhancements as well as usage of origami the wearable sensor will be least 4 times more accurate. Data collected from authors was used to construct a graph showing correlation between the voltage production and glucose concentration, using a conventional glucose detector to compare the accuracy. The coefficient of determination was around 0.972 showing a direct relationship between glucose concentration and voltage production. This work is the first-ever reported to incorporate chemical enhancements and origami designs into a wearable glucose sensor during exercise.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Distributed Shock Wave Localization System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: To achieve high-precision detection of ammunition detonation/impact points over a large area, a distributed shockwave localization system has been designed, which employs shockwave arrival times to estimate trajectories and determine impact locations. The system adopts a single-element array structure, automatically acquiring precise absolute timing, its spatial coordinates, and the relative positions of each element. It features a self-triggered recording of both the arrival moments of ballistic shockwaves and their complete waveforms. All measuring devices and control centers are remotely controlled and data is transmitted through a dedicated 4G network. The measurement device is compact, energy-efficient, and adaptable, with the capability to monitor power levels, and its orientation, among other parameters, making it suitable for unmanned scenarios requiring wide-area measurements. Field tests conducted at a firing range using static explosion experiments validated the system’s functionality, successfully obtaining accurate arrival times and complete shockwave waveform data. The experimental outcomes demonstrated that the system operates reliably, provides accurate measurements, and possesses practical application capabilities, highlighting its efficacy in real-world scenarios demanding precise detection of ammunition impact locations across expansive territories.

articleTitle: Analysis of Polarization Error of the Half-Wave Plate in Photon-Entangled Fiber Optic Gyroscope
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: This paper derives the principle of the photon-entangled fiber gyro’s optical path, simulates and compares the effect of the rotation angle of the half-wave plate (HWP) optical axis on the output state quantum interference efficiency, and performs a simulation analysis of the polarization entanglement error in the photon-entangled fiber gyro. It is proven that the rotation angle of the half-wave plate’s optical axis has a significant impact on the quantum interference efficiency, with the maximum quantum interference efficiency corresponding to a half-wave plate optical axis rotation angle of 22.5°. When there is a deviation in the rotation angles of the two half-wave plates, it does not lead to non-reciprocal phase errors.Still, it lowers quantum interference efficiency and increases measurement difficulty. Excessive errors in the rotation angle of the half-wave plate’s optical axis may reduce the accuracy performance of the gyroscope. The polarization error generated by the entire optical path may lead to the inability to break through the shot noise limit (SNL), and in the case of existing background noise, the polarization error has a more severe impact on the accuracy of the entangled gyroscope.

articleTitle: Vehicle-mounted SINS/Dual LDV Integrated Navigation Method Based on Sequential Residual Chi-square Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: The laser Doppler velocimeter (LDV) has been widely used in vehicle integrated navigation with strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS). However, the traditional SINS/LDV vehicle integrated navigation system can not work normally in the unfavorable navigation environment such as stagnant water and mud, because the LDV is prone to measurement failure when it encounters the above unfavorable roads. In this paper, a method that SINS/dual LDV integrated navigation based on sequential residual chi-square detection is proposed to meet the demand of military vehicles for on-board navigation system with high precision, high reliability and high concealment. Firstly, the velocity measurement error model of LDV is considered. Then the 21-dimensional SINS/dual LDV integrated navigation system model is constructed by speed combination. Finally, the validity of LDV output speed is judged by chi-square fault detection algorithm, and the fault information is eliminated by sequential filtering, so that the integrated navigation system with high robustness is obtained. The results of the vehicle-based experiments indicate that the designed SINS/dual LDV integrated navigation system can still maintain a high level of positioning accuracy even when a single set of LDV experiences a long-duration measurement failure.

articleTitle: Automatic Signal Recognition Methods of Interferometric Optical Fiber Sensor Array Based on Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Because of the polymorphism of the array signal, there is a big error in the recognition of the array signal. Therefore, an automatic recognition method of interferometric fiber sensor array signal based on support vector machine is proposed. On the analysis of the interferometric sensing technology, on the basis of the running mechanism, the short-time logarithm energy extraction of the array signal is realized, and based on the related parameters, it is set to improve the effect of signal acquisition. SVM is used to analyze the array signal decomposition; the decomposition is obtained by using the variational iteration search model modal component of center frequency and bandwidth. On this basis, signal recognition is realized by the repetition rate feature and small window repetition rate feature. The test results show that the recognition accuracy of the design method is above 97%, and it has a good application effect.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Position Movement of the Accelerations Sensors on Seat of A Human Centrifuge for System Accelerations Errors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: With the improving of training demand of pilot anti-overload ability and the development of new fighter jets with their supporting anti G equipments,the human-machine engineering problems caused by the existing seat on human centrifuge are becoming increasingly prominent, which are difficult to meet practical need and need to be upgraded. After upgrading, the seat can be quickly adjusted in front and back, up and down. The acceleration sensors fixed on the seat will also generate displacement, resulting in errors. The three-axis acceleration values are important technical indicators in centrifuge system, and its errors need to be within a certain accuracy range in order to make the system operate normally. Otherwise, the system will produce serious consequences such as alarm and shutdown. In this study the maximum values of acceleration errors in seat adjustment are calculated and discussed in detail, and the magnitude of acceleration errors caused by the position displacement of accelerations sensors due to seat position adjustment, as well as the impact of these errors on the system are calculated and discussed. The result indicates that, the accelerations errors caused by the up and down adjustment of the upgraded seat have any adverse effects on control system. For safety system, three-axis acceleration errors need to be calculated carefully, and are observed that if the values are within limits set by safety system, to determine if acceleration errors will produce effect on the safety of the whole system.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of UWB Indoor Positioning Based on Two-Layer Bi-Directional GRU Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: Ultra-wideband technology is characterized by fast transmission speed and strong anti-interference ability, so it is widely used in high-precision indoor positioning. However, when ultra-wideband technology is used for indoor environment localization, the presence of non-line-of-sight, multi-path and other interference factors seriously affects the ultra-wideband ranging accuracy and signal stability. In order to improve the problem of declining localization accuracy of ultra-wideband technology in complex environments, this paper proposes a localization method based on the bi-layer bi-directional gated cyclic cell network model, which utilizes the time-position sequence characteristics of the locating target’s dynamic motion, the motion features are extracted from historical data, and the network structure parameters are designed to verify its effectiveness. The experimental results show that the ultrawideband localization accuracy based on this GRU model is improved by 56.75%, 50.64%, and 18.2% compared with polynomial fitting algorithm, unidirectional GRU model, and bidirectional GRU model, respectively, and the localization effect is better.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies of Granary Clearing Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Sensor Technology and Control (ISSTC)
abstract: As an automated device specifically designed for the warehousing industry, granary clearing machines can significantly improve the low efficiency of manual clearing, effectively reduce safety risks during manual operations, lower costs, and ensure more efficient and safer operations. However, the current granary clearing machines on the market have a low level of automation, and some operational steps still require manual intervention. To address this issue, this paper first classifies and discusses the granary clearing machines currently in use. Secondly, it proposes the system composition and design plan for an intelligent clearing robot. Finally, it optimizes key technologies such as machine vision and multi-sensor fusion algorithms to address the unique environment inside granaries, enhancing the robot’s capabilities in recognition, perception, and operation. Through research on the key technologies of granary clearing robots, we aim to develop more intelligent, efficient, and safe machines to meet the needs of smart warehouse management in granaries. This research is expected to provide insights for the future development of intelligent clearing machines and smart grain storage systems.
